top_news.title: LLM Usage in Debian: Three Proposals
top_news.dek: The Debian project is currently evaluating multiple formal proposals regarding the integration and usage of LLMs within its distribution.
top_news.brief: Debian developers are debating how to handle LLM-related software and AI-generated content within the ecosystem. The project has opened a formal voting process to determine the community's stance on these technologies, with several distinct proposals currently under consideration by the project members.

top_news.title: The AI coding tutor paradox grows as educators scramble to rethink how they test real skills
top_news.dek: A global survey of 763 computer science educators reveals that 68% have overhauled assessment methods due to AI coding tools.
top_news.brief: Educators are shifting away from traditional coding assignments toward oral exams, proctored tests, and project-based assessments to ensure students actually understand programming concepts. Despite these changes, nearly half of the surveyed faculty report a lack of established frameworks or examples for effectively integrating AI into their curricula.

top_news.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
top_news.dek: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 5, a new flagship model that currently leads the Artificial Analysis leaderboard.
top_news.brief: Claude Opus 5 is positioned as a highly capable model, reportedly matching the frontier intelligence of Claude Fable 5 while being offered at a lower price point. It maintains the same pricing structure as its predecessor, Opus 4.8, and includes a fast-mode option for improved latency.

primary.title: Opus 5 may have solved browser-based prompt injection, the biggest security flaw haunting AI agents
primary.summary: Opus 5 combined with Auto Mode hits a zero percent prompt injection success rate for browser agents across 129 test scenarios. Without those extra protection layers, the rate is 3.7 percent. If these numbers hold up in practice, Anthropic may have cracked one of the biggest security problems facing AI agents that operate in browsers. The article Opus 5 may have solved browser-based prompt injection, the biggest security flaw haunting AI agents appeared first on The Decoder.
